factual_methodology.summary: BLS, Federal Reserve, TreasuryDirect, China's National Bureau of Statistics, ECB, OPEC, TSE and BCB provide the primary policy and macro evidence. Intraday Treasury, equity and oil observations are clearly time-bounded and supported separately.

novelty.summary: The 6 October analytical delta moves beyond the prior day's activity-versus-prices divergence. The lead is now the split between softer front-end policy expectations and a still-expensive long end, with oil easing, China stabilizing and Brazil's electoral repricing awaiting fiscal confirmation.

editorial_publication_readiness.summary: The brief separates official macro releases from market observations, identifies the information cutoff, avoids treating a single Brazilian trading session as a policy forecast and states explicit invalidation conditions.

contextual_depth.summary: The brief links labour cooling, the Treasury term premium, energy transmission, Chinese stabilization, euro-area financing conditions and Brazil's political risk through explicit mechanisms and second-order effects.

visual_evidence_readiness.signature: 1 evidence table + 4 explicit charts + 1 causal flow + 1 regional transmission map per locale
visual_evidence_readiness.summary: Visual floor for a brief is exceeded. Treasury yields are charted in common units; China PMI measures share an index scale; euro-area inflation and borrowing-cost values are explicitly caveated as different concepts; Brazil vote shares use TSE percentages.
visual_evidence_readiness.limitations: Treasury and oil observations are intraday. The euro-area chart places inflation and borrowing rates on the same percentage scale only for compact comparison, not to imply identical economic meaning.

contrary_evidence: Lower oil prices reduce part of the near-term inflation impulse and could help long yields stabilize if the decline persists.
Weak U.S. payroll growth and softer short-rate expectations could eventually pull the long end lower if activity deteriorates more broadly.
China's official PMI is only marginally above 50, while smaller manufacturers and non-manufacturing new orders remain weak.
Brazil's initial post-election asset repricing can reverse if fiscal commitments or coalition signals disappoint.
limitations: Market prices cited for 6 October are early-session observations and can change materially before the close.
The article does not treat the Treasury term premium as directly observed; it is an analytical interpretation of curve behavior, inflation uncertainty, fiscal supply and duration risk.
China PMI diffusion indexes indicate breadth and direction rather than direct output growth rates.
The 5 October Focus survey reflects responses collected before Brazil's first-round election and is used only to identify the information lag between expectations and market repricing.
notes: Approved for same-day publication with an 08:45 BRT information cutoff. EN/PT-BR parity and controlled geography/taxonomy were checked before public materialization.

en.title: Global Macro — long yields become the constraint as oil eases and risk assets keep testing the cost of capital
en.deck: Long U.S. yields remain near multi-decade highs even as oil eases below the recent risk peak, equities stay resilient, China stabilizes and Brazil absorbs a post-election repricing shock.
en.regime: Long-duration financing costs have become the main macro constraint: labour is cooling and oil is easing, but long U.S. yields remain above 5% while global activity avoids a synchronized contraction.
en.key_risk: A persistent term premium above 5% can tighten credit and valuation conditions even without additional short-rate tightening, turning a resilient nominal-growth regime into a balance-sheet and refinancing problem.

pt-BR.title: Macro Global — juros longos viram a restrição central enquanto petróleo alivia e ativos de risco testam o custo de capital
pt-BR.deck: Juros longos dos EUA continuam perto das máximas de décadas mesmo com petróleo abaixo do pico recente, ações resilientes, China estabilizando e Brasil absorvendo o choque de repricing pós-eleição.
pt-BR.regime: O custo de financiamento de longa duração virou a principal restrição macro: o trabalho esfria e o petróleo alivia, mas juros longos dos EUA seguem acima de 5% enquanto a atividade global evita contração sincronizada.
pt-BR.key_risk: Prêmio de prazo persistentemente acima de 5% pode apertar crédito e valuations mesmo sem novo aumento da taxa curta, transformando um regime de crescimento nominal resiliente em problema de balanço e refinanciamento.
